problem.title: Many companies don't know what they're exposing
problem.subtitle: A visible service or outdated setting can go unnoticed. An initial external assessment helps you decide where to look.

exposedServices.title: Exposed services without protection

sslTls.title: Misconfigured SSL/TLS certificates
sslTls.description: Expired certificates, obsolete protocols, or weak configurations that compromise communication security.

vulnerabilities.title: Unpatched known vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Documented software security flaws (CVEs) that may affect observed versions and need verification.

configurations.title: Insecure configurations
configurations.description: Default settings, missing web protection headers or access that is broader than necessary.

database.title: A database service responds from the Internet
database.meaning: The MySQL service is accessible externally. This does not demonstrate an intrusion, but it is worth confirming whether this access is needed.
database.nextStep: Ask your technical contact to verify public access and consider restricting it to authorized networks. Repeat the assessment after any changes.

https.title: No policy requiring HTTPS is observed
https.meaning: The example web response does not include the HSTS header. Browsers may not receive the instruction to always use an encrypted connection.
https.nextStep: Discuss whether to enable HSTS after checking the domain works correctly over HTTPS. Validate the scope before including subdomains.

faq.title: What to expect from Odimetry
faq.description: A useful tool starts by explaining what it observes and what is outside its scope.

audience.question: Do I need cybersecurity expertise?
audience.answer: Not to understand the assessment summary. Odimetry is designed for small businesses and self-employed professionals, with or without a technical background. Findings include context and priorities; verifying or making changes may require your technical team or provider.

scope.question: Can I assess any domain?
scope.answer: No. Only assess domains and assets that you own or have explicit permission to assess. Define the authorized scope before starting an assessment.

limits.question: What are the limits of an external assessment?
limits.answer: It reflects signals observable at the time of analysis and within the authorized scope. Results can change and do not necessarily detect every vulnerability. It does not guarantee freedom from incidents or replace a full internal audit, a manual penetration test or continuous monitoring.

certification.question: Does a report certify security or compliance?
certification.answer: No. Odimetry does not certify security or establish ISO 27001 or other regulatory compliance. Findings and recommendations are indicative and require review in the context of your organization.

availability.question: Is Odimetry commercially available yet?
availability.answer: Odimetry is in development and market validation. To receive updates, leave your email in the interest section.
